rules.name: Rapid onward movement

facts.text: TXN-4001680: ₹30,000 left ACC-100209 7.0 min later (cumulative 60% of the receipt).
TXN-4001681: ₹20,000 left ACC-100209 13.0 min later (cumulative 100% of the receipt).
Threshold met: ≥80% moved on within 60 min.

limitations: Shows recorded onward transfers; whether they carried the disputed funds is given by attribution, not by timing.
rules.suggested_step: Review attribution bounds and consider a hold on visible downstream accounts still holding funds.

rules.name: Split into multiple transfers

facts.text: 2 onward transfers to 2 distinct accounts within 120 min, totalling ₹50,000 (100% of the receipt).

limitations: Splitting is common in legitimate use (rent, bills); it is a pattern to review, not evidence of intent.
rules.suggested_step: Check each destination account's ownership and whether destinations appear in other disputes.

rules.name: Beneficiary linked to other disputes

facts.text: ACC-100209 is the beneficiary in 2 other dispute(s): CASE-24031, CASE-24038.

limitations: Only disputes recorded in this system are compared; other banks' reports are not visible.
rules.suggested_step: Open the linked cases and compare allegations; consider a coordinated hold request.

rules.name: Failed logins before the transfer

facts.text: 4 failed and 1 successful authentication events in the 30 min before the transfer.
Success at 17:36 followed 4 failures; the transfer followed 8.0 min later.

limitations: Failed attempts can be the genuine customer mistyping; combine with device and location evidence.
rules.suggested_step: Compare the device and IP of the successful login with the customer's usual devices.

rules.name: New device

facts.text: Device DEV-9071 was first used on ACC-100216 0.2 h before the disputed transfer (history checked: 180 days).

limitations: Customers do change phones; a new device on the account is a signal, not proof of account takeover.
rules.suggested_step: Ask the customer whether they registered a new device; check SIM-swap indicators with the telecom partner.

rules.name: Unusual amount

facts.text: Disputed amount ₹50,000 is 24.7× the payer's median debit of ₹2,025 over 14 debits in 90 days.

limitations: Large one-off payments (deposits, purchases) are normal; baseline is this bank's records only.
rules.suggested_step: Ask the customer about any expected large payments around this date.

rules.name: Recently opened beneficiary

facts.text: Beneficiary ACC-100209 was opened 8 day(s) before receiving the funds.

limitations: New accounts are mostly legitimate; this matters in combination with rapid onward movement.
rules.suggested_step: Review beneficiary KYC and recent inflow pattern.

rules.name: Reversal then resend

facts.text: No reversal followed by a resend on the payer's account within ±24 h.

limitations: Reversals happen for technical reasons; check the reversal reason codes.
rules.suggested_step: Check reversal reason codes and whether the customer initiated the resend.

rules.name: Evidence contradicts the ledger
limitations: Not evaluable: the data this rule needs is missing. This is not a negative finding.
rules.suggested_step: Ask the customer for the payment receipt or statement and analyse it.

rules.name: Shared device

facts.text: Device DEV-9071 is also used by 1 other account(s): ACC-100214.

rules.suggested_step: Check whether the other accounts belong to the same household or appear in disputes.

rules.name: Funds left this bank

facts.text: Between ₹20,000 and ₹20,000 of the disputed funds may have left to ACC-100211 (Other Bank A (synthetic)); this bank cannot see further.
Between ₹9,800 and ₹12,000 of the disputed funds may have left to ACC-100212 (Other Bank B (synthetic)); this bank cannot see further.

limitations: Exits end this bank's visibility; the trail continues only with the receiving institution's records.
rules.suggested_step: Send a trail and hold request to the receiving institution (via the national cyber-fraud reporting process).

rules.name: Record inconsistency

facts.text: All 4 trail records have unique, consistent references.

limitations: Missing references are often a data-feed issue, not fraud.
rules.suggested_step: Reconcile the records with the payment switch using amount, time and parties.
